docs.title: Appztore Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the Appztore documentation!

Appztore is an open-source, universal package and application orchestrator for Linux desktops. It bridges the gap across fragmented software distribution channels by unifying:

  • Arch Linux / Pacman (Official Repositories)
  • AUR (Arch User Repository) via yay / paru
  • Flatpak / Flathub
  • Snapcraft
  • Docker Hub

docs.title: 🌟 Key Highlights
docs.text:
• Multi-Registry Search: Search packages across all supported package managers simultaneously in real time.
  • Pure OS Fallback: Zero external API dependencies needed for core registry searches; utilizes native binaries (pacman, flatpak, yay, etc.).
  • Security Audit Scoring: Visual safety tiers based on repository provenance, confinement levels, and integrity checks.
  • Strict Command Injection Guard: Regex-driven input validation preventing malicious operators (;&|) from executing in root/privileged contexts.
  • Telemetry Stream: Live terminal output streaming directly into the desktop UI during installations.
  • AI Intent Search (Optional): Natural language querying to discover tools by intent using LiteLLM/Groq.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Desktop Application Guide: Explore the desktop UI, package filters, and telemetry viewer.
  • CLI & TUI Guide: Work with command-line workflows and system integration.
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP): Connect Appztore with LLM agents.
  • System Architecture: Deep-dive into the Tauri v2, Python backend, and IPC design.

docs.title: 🛠️ Quick Installation
docs.text:
For pre-built releases:

# AppImage (Universal Linux)
chmod +x appztore_1.0.1_amd64.AppImage
./appztore_1.0.1_amd64.AppImage

# Debian / Ubuntu (.deb)
sudo dpkg -i appztore_1.0.1_amd64.deb

# Fedora / RHEL (.rpm)
sudo rpm -i appztore-1.0.1-1.x86_64.rpm

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
Appztore is designed as a hybrid desktop application combining a low-overhead native window shell, a high-performance React UI, and a Python core service.

flowchart TD
    subgraph UI ["Frontend (React 19 + Vite)"]
        A[Search & Filter Controls] --> B[Telemetry Viewer SSE]
        A --> C[Security Badge Display]
    end

    subgraph Tauri ["Tauri v2 OS Bridge (Rust)"]
        D[Window Manager]
        E[Privileged Command Execution]
        F[System Tray & Notifications]
    end

    subgraph Backend ["Core Service (Python Flask)"]
        G[REST API & SSE Endpoints]
        H[Multi-threaded Registry Dispatcher]
        I[Command Injection Validator]
        J[LiteLLM Intent Resolver]
    end

    subgraph Registries ["System Drivers & Registries"]
        K[Pacman]
        L[AUR / Yay]
        M[Flatpak]
        N[Snapcraft]
        O[Docker Hub]
    end

    UI <-->|HTTP / SSE / Tauri IPC| Tauri
    Tauri <-->|Localhost REST / Port 5001| Backend
    Backend --> I
    I --> H
    H --> K
    H --> L
    H --> M
    H --> N
    H --> O
    Backend --> J

docs.title: 1. Frontend Layer (desktop-app/src)
docs.text:
• React 19 with TypeScript for reactive state and type-safe component hierarchy.
  • Tailwind CSS with Dark UI theme tailored for Linux power users.
  • Framer Motion for smooth transition animations.
  • Virtual Scrolling via react-window to handle thousands of search results smoothly without DOM lag.

docs.title: 2. Native Bridge Layer (desktop-app/src-tauri)
docs.text:
• Built on Tauri v2 using Rust.
  • Spawns the backend Python microservice on startup and terminates it cleanly on exit.
  • Manages native dialogs, system tray menus, and privileged execution bridging via pkexec.

docs.title: 3. Backend Engine (backend/app)
docs.text:
• Parallel Dispatch: Searches across all package managers concurrently using a ThreadPoolExecutor.
  • In-Memory TTL Cache: Fast caching of search queries to eliminate duplicate shell calls and reduce latency.
  • Strict Sanitization: Every command is validated against malicious shell injection patterns before return.
  • Fallback Resilience: If an external LLM fails or no API keys exist, the engine seamlessly degrades to fast native OS searches.

docs.title: CLI & TUI Workflows
docs.text: In addition to the graphical desktop app, Appztore supports scriptable terminal workflows and seamless integration with command-line tools.

docs.title: 💻 Pure OS Fallback Mode
docs.text:
Appztore can operate in environments without external internet API keys or LLM backends.

When running in pure OS mode, Appztore uses native distribution binaries: - pacman -Ss <query> for Arch official packages. - yay -Ss <query> or paru -Ss <query> for AUR packages. - flatpak search <query> for Flathub remotes. - snap find <query> for Canonical Snap Store. - docker search <query> for Docker Hub images.

docs.title: 🛡️ Input Sanitization & Security
docs.text:
All commands constructed or suggested by Appztore pass through strict regex verification:

# Disallowed characters & patterns:
# - Shell chaining: ; && ||
# - Redirection: | > <
# - Command substitution: ` $( )

This prevents accidental or malicious command execution when escalating permissions via pkexec or sudo.

docs.title: 🚀 Environment Flags
docs.text:
You can customize backend behaviors using environment variables:

Variable Description Default LITELLM_MODEL AI model to use for intent extraction groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile GROQ_API_KEY API key for Groq LLM queries None PORT Backend service HTTP port 5001 DEBUG Enable debug logging false

docs.title: Desktop Application
docs.text: The Appztore desktop client is built on Tauri v2 with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. It provides a fast, lightweight, and modern graphical interface for discovering, inspecting, and installing Linux software.

docs.title: 1. Unified Search Bar
docs.text:
• Keyword Search: Type any package name (e.g. vlc, neovim, firefox).
  • Natural Language Intent: Query by description (e.g., "video editor with GPU acceleration" or "markdown note-taking tool").
  • Fast Local Indexing: Results from cached and local binary searches appear instantaneously.

docs.title: 2. Registry Filter Tabs
docs.text: Easily toggle or isolate results from specific package sources: - All Sources: Merged view deduplicating identical applications across sources. - Pacman: Arch Linux official binary repositories. - AUR: Community packages built from source via yay/paru. - Flatpak: Sandboxed applications from Flathub. - Snapcraft: Snaps with canonical confinement. - Docker: Containerized applications and server utilities.

docs.title: 3. Security Audit Badges
docs.text: Every package card displays a security rating and verification badge: - Arch Official (95%): GPG-signed binary package from official maintainers. - Docker Official (90%): Verified Docker Hub official image. - Flathub (88%): Sandboxed flatpak with security manifest inspection. - Snapcraft (85%): Canonical snap with confinement guarantees. - AUR Community (75%): User-submitted PKGBUILD requiring community review.

docs.title: 4. Real-Time Installation Telemetry
docs.text: When an installation is triggered: - An inline terminal modal opens. - Output from pkexec / pacman / flatpak is streamed line-by-line using Server-Sent Events (SSE). - Errors and warnings are highlighted automatically for quick troubleshooting.

docs.title: ⌨️ Desktop Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl + K / Cmd + K Focus search bar Escape Close modals / Clear active search Ctrl + R Refresh registry indexes Tab Cycle through registry filter tabs

docs.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
docs.text: Appztore provides native compatibility with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing AI assistants and coding agents to query package registries, check installation statuses, and safely manage applications on Linux systems.

docs.title: search_packages
docs.text:
Search across Pacman, Flatpak, AUR, Snapcraft, and Docker Hub.

Parameters: - query (string, required): Package name or descriptive intent (e.g., "audio workstation"). - registry (string, optional): Specific registry filter ("pacman", "flatpak", "aur", "snap", "docker", or "all").

docs.title: get_app_details
docs.text:
Retrieve detailed metadata, security scores, and installation command recipes for an application.

Parameters: - app_id (string, required): Identifier of the application (e.g., "org.videolan.VLC" or "arch:neovim").

docs.title: verify_command
docs.text:
Check whether a package installation command adheres to strict command sanitization rules.

Parameters: - command (string, required): Shell command string to validate.

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration Example
docs.text:
Add Appztore as an MCP server in your MCP client configuration (e.g. Claude Desktop or Antigravity):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "appztore": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["backend/app/main.py"],
      "env": {
        "PORT": "5001"
      }
    }
  }
}
